claims.text: single oral dose of doxycycline within 72 hours of removal for high-risk Ixodes bites, all age groups
claims.quote: For high-risk Ixodes spp. bites in all age groups, we recommend the administration of a single dose of oral doxycycline within 72 hours of tick removal over observation

claims.text: high-risk bite = identified Ixodes vector, highly endemic area, attached >=36 hours; criteria apply to any Ixodes species
claims.quote: the tick bite was from (a) an identified Ixodes spp. vector species, (b) it occurred in a highly endemic area, and (c) the tick was attached for ≥36 hours.

claims.text: guidelines recommend against prophylaxis for equivocal or low-risk bites
claims.quote: but not for bites that are equivocal risk or low risk

claims.text: wait-and-watch approach when a bite cannot be classified as high-risk
claims.quote: If a tick bite cannot be classified with a high level of certainty as a high-risk bite, a wait-and-watch approach is recommended.

claims.text: dose 200 mg adults, 4.4 mg/kg up to 200 mg for children
claims.quote: Doxycycline is given as a single oral dose, 200 mg for adults and 4.4 mg/kg (up to a maximum dose of 200 mg) for children.

claims.text: most B. burgdorferi transmission occurs after 36 to 48 hours of attachment
claims.quote: the majority of transmission occurs after 36–48 hours of attachment

claims.quote: we advise pregnant women to have an informed discussion with their physicians about the risks, benefits

claims.text: IDSA endorses single-dose prophylaxis for high-risk bites
claims.quote: (strong recommendation, moderate-quality evidence)

claims.text: doxycycline needed if Anaplasma coinfection is suspected
claims.quote: which, if suspected, would necessitate the use of doxycycline

claims.text: neurologic Lyme without brain or spinal cord involvement: IV ceftriaxone, cefotaxime, penicillin G or oral doxycycline, 14 to 21 days
claims.quote: we recommend using intravenous (IV) ceftriaxone, cefotaxime, penicillin G, or oral doxycycline over other antimicrobials ... The preferred antibiotic duration is 14–21 days.

claims.text: brain or spinal cord parenchymal involvement: IV over oral
claims.quote: we recommend using IV over oral antibiotics

claims.text: carditis: oral for outpatients, initial IV ceftriaxone for hospitalized until improvement, 14 to 21 days total
claims.quote: we suggest oral antibiotics over IV antibiotics ... we suggest initially using IV ceftriaxone over oral antibiotics until there is evidence of clinical improvement ... we suggest 14–21 days of total antibiotic therapy

claims.text: persistent nonspecific symptoms without objective evidence of reinfection or failure: against additional antibiotics
claims.quote: we recommend against additional antibiotic therapy

claims.text: investigate coinfection if persistent fever >1 day on Lyme treatment
claims.quote: Coinfection should be investigated in patients who have a persistent fever for >1 day while on antibiotic treatment for Lyme disease.

claims.text: guidelines give stage-specific recommendations
